problems.verifierReason: Formula applies to thin sinusoidal phase gratings, not amplitude gratings.

problems.quote: "She will either call or email" omits the object after email (which can be a verb), creating a shift in parts of speech
problems.problem: If 'email' is a verb, 'call' and 'email' are both verbs, so there is no shift in parts of speech; the object is ellipted from both conjuncts.
problems.correction: "She will either call or email" is parallel when both are verbs; no shift occurs
problems.verifierReason: Both 'call' and 'email' function as verbs with ellipted objects; no POS shift.

problems.quote: The preferred reading in formal writing is the narrow scope of negation over the quantifier
problems.problem: The phrase 'narrow scope of negation over the quantifier' is terminologically contradictory. In formal semantics, the preferred reading of 'Every student did not pass' is the surface scope where the quantifier takes wide scope over negation (∀x ¬P(x)), not a narrow scope of negation over the quantif
problems.correction: The preferred reading in formal writing gives the quantifier wide scope over negation (∀x ¬P(x))
problems.verifierReason: Preferred reading of 'Every student did not pass' is ∀x¬P(x) (quantifier wide scope).

problems.quote: Certain markers are restricted to clause‑initial position ( however )
problems.problem: 'However' is not restricted to clause-initial position; it can appear medially as a parenthetical (e.g., 'The results, however, were encouraging'). The restriction is that it must not be preceded by only a comma when joining independent clauses.
problems.correction: Certain markers like 'however' must not be preceded by a comma when joining independent clauses
problems.verifierReason: 'However' can appear medially; the real restriction is no comma-only before it when joining independent clauses.

problems.quote: object relatives (* the report the analyst wrote ) do not reduce in standard English
problems.problem: Object relative clauses do reduce in standard English by omitting the relative pronoun (zero relativization); the example given is grammatical.
problems.correction: object relatives reduce via zero relativization (e.g., the report the analyst wrote)
problems.verifierReason: Object relative clauses can omit the pronoun (zero relativization) in standard English; the correction is accurate.
